definition.name: diamond_distance
definition.definition: The diamond distance (or diamond norm) between two quantum channels Phi, Psi is ||Phi - Psi||_diamond = sup_{rho >= 0, tr(rho)=1} ||(Phi tensor id_d)(rho) - (Psi tensor id_d)(rho)||_1, where the supremum is over all bipartite states on the system plus an equally-sized ancilla. The diamond distance captures the worst-case distinguishability of two channels, accounting for entanglement with a reference system. A channel is implemented 'to delta error in diamond distance' if the actual implementation Phi_impl satisfies ||Phi - Phi_impl||_diamond <= delta.
